topic.title: Latent Confounding and Causal Model Identifiability
topic.overview: Causal discovery becomes harder when important variables are unobserved. This topic studies when causal structures or their numerical parameters can still be recovered using distributional assumptions, proxy measurements, temporal information, or special graphical conditions. A representative analysis separates different parameter ambiguities in partially observed linear models and identifies conditions that resolve them.
topic.whyItMatters: Hidden variables can make several causal explanations observationally equivalent. Identifiability results show which conclusions follow from the evidence and which depend on assumptions that prediction accuracy alone cannot validate.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives connect causal parameter estimation with learning rules and non-Gaussian temporal models. Later work expands to nonlinear confounders and causal disentanglement. Recent spatial methods use neighboring treatments as proxies for latent confounding while explicitly accounting for interference, alongside robustness studies of noise and temporal distributions.
openQuestions: Which latent-variable assumptions have observable implications that can be checked?
How sensitive are recovered structures and effects to imperfect proxies or misspecified noise models?

papers.tldr: A latent-confounder extension of Poisson branching causal models characterizes local three-variable identifiability and supports practical structure learning.

papers.title: Power-Boosted Granger-Causal Discovery for Large Heterogeneous Panel Data
papers.tldr: PE-PGCT enhances existing panel Granger tests, especially for high-dimensional or sparse signals, with asymptotically negligible null size distortion.

papers.title: Robust Causal Discovery in Real-World Time Series with Power-Laws
papers.tldr: Power-law spectral features improve reported causal discovery performance on noisy synthetic and real-world time series.

papers.title: Skewness-Robust Causal Discovery in Location-Scale Noise Models
papers.tldr: SkewD extends location-scale causal discovery to skew-normal noise, addressing performance losses caused by assuming symmetric variation.

papers.title: Spatial Deconfounder: Interference-Aware Deconfounding for Spatial Causal Inference
papers.tldr: The Spatial Deconfounder uses local treatment patterns to reconstruct hidden spatial confounding and estimate direct and spillover effects.
